task: Collect edition-bound CPIN footnotes and retrieve deduplicated cited HTML and PDF sources with robots and resumable provenance

candidates.fit: Reuse existing robots, host delays, refusal handling, hashes and page text extraction.
candidates.scope: Local CPIN retrieval and PDF text, not evidence interpretation.
candidates.limits: Existing client has no streaming size bound or cross-host coordinator; existing PDF method is CPIN-specific and must not be rewritten for external sources. Sustained use of new collection workflow is unknown.
candidates.licence: Owner-owned CPIN code; already-installed httpx/lxml/PyMuPDF licensing unchanged. PyMuPDF is an existing dependency.
candidates.maintenance: Current main 4147628; maintained locally; tests/test_http.py covers refusals and robots failures.
candidates.adaptation: Add optional bounded streaming and URL guard, leaving old callers unchanged. Keep external-source PDF extraction separate, with PyMuPDF used only from the main thread.
candidates.transfer: Preserve immutable documents and failed attempts; never treat retrieval failures as contradictory evidence.
candidates.recommendation: Reuse client and installed PDF library; directly implement catalogue and a resumable, bounded scheduler.

sources.observation: Robots refusals, read failures and per-host delays are already handled.
Repeatable mock checks cover refused/unreadable robots and National Archives stop rule.
Page text extraction preserves a page-level source location; layout is not semantic evidence.

candidates.fit: Contained HTML text extractor removes article boilerplate more cheaply than a new heuristic subsystem.
candidates.scope: Extraction only; use CPIN client for all network activity.
candidates.limits: Main text can be omitted or flattened, as operator issue 883 reports. Sustained production evidence not established within this short scan; retain original bytes and mark extraction as unverified.
candidates.licence: Apache-2.0 for versions from 1.8; official repository licence inspected.
candidates.maintenance: Active official documentation and maintainer repository; candidate version will be recorded after install.
candidates.adaptation: One bounded optional source-collection dependency. Pin major version; retain raw HTML so extraction can be replaced without another scrape.
candidates.transfer: Use extraction with tables and no comments; retain provenance and test representative HTML/PDF. Do not use crawler or fetching helpers.
candidates.recommendation: Adopt extraction as a tested pilot component, without calling it operational.

sources.observation: Repository confirms modular extraction and Apache-2.0 licence.
Extract accepts raw HTML; precision/recall choices and possible omissions documented.
Operator reports flattened document structure; this is a limitation rather than proof of sustained reliability.
Use inventory lists integrations but does not independently prove their sustained operation.

decision.choice: Reuse CPIN PoliteClient and installed PyMuPDF; add Trafilatura for HTML extraction and implement only source/claim indexing plus resumable coordination.
decision.rationale: Direct custom HTML extraction would save a dependency but add boilerplate heuristics and maintenance. Existing scraper removes most network infrastructure work. No new browser scraper, RAG framework or AI provider is needed for retrieval.
decision.own_work_checked: Current CPIN HTTP/linkcheck/PDF code and installed versions inspected. Bounded local catalogue found no extra match; owned GitHub list screened and unrelated macro/music/conversion repos rejected before deep inspection.
decision.stop_reason: Stopped after roughly seven minutes; enough evidence to choose existing retrieval plus contained extraction, and further repository hunting is unlikely to save work.
decision.next_check: Install recorded extraction version, run fixture tests and a representative real-source pilot before the full run.
decision.limitations: Public discovery returned no matching external repository; official library sources inspected separately. No candidate promoted to sustained operational status. Public HTML/PDF extraction is fallible, some linked addresses are malformed, robots/auth/refusals prevent complete retrieval. Private source cache is excluded from site builds and model inputs.
